example_prompt: Add a Djomy webhook handler to automatically confirm orders when payment completes.

input_schema.description: Payload Djomy POSTs to your webhook URL when a payment event occurs.

eventType.description: Type of event. Use payment.success as the trigger to call verify_payment. payout.* events are sent only with a V2 webhook configuration.

eventId.description: Unique identifier for this webhook event.

data.description: Shape depends on the payload version of the webhook configuration (Djomy developer space). V2 — default for new configurations: the payment under data.payment (payment.* events) or the payout under data.payout (payout.* events), never both. V1 — merchants integrated before V2: the payment fields directly in data (same fields as data.payment), payment.* events only.

transactionId.description: Unique payment identifier — pass it to verify_payment.

fees.description: Fees taken from the paid amount.

paymentMethod.description: e.g. OM (Orange Money), MOMO (MTN Mobile Money), KULU.

providerReference.description: Reference of the payment provider (Orange Money, Kulu…).

payout.description: V2, payout.* events. Payouts have no spec in this registry.

paymentLinkReference.description: Reference of the payment link associated with this event, if applicable.

timestamp.description: ISO 8601 timestamp when the event occurred.

metadata.description: Custom data passed by the merchant when creating the payment.

response_schema.description: Return HTTP 200. The docs list 200, 400 and 500 responses; what Djomy does with the body or with a failed delivery is not documented (see open_questions).

gotchas: [MUST TELL USER] The Djomy webhook does not fire on its own. The developer must first set their endpoint URL in the Djomy dashboard (developer area). Without this step, no event is sent, even when the payment succeeds.

[MUST TELL USER] Djomy cannot reach localhost, and its docs require HTTPS for returnUrl and cancelUrl (they say nothing about the webhook URL). In local development, tell the user explicitly: run `ngrok http 3000`, then set the HTTPS ngrok URL in the Djomy developer area before testing.
Verify X-Webhook-Signature as described in webhook.signature before processing the event; ignore the webhook if it does not match or if the version prefix is not v1.

Read the payment from data.payment with a V2 webhook configuration (the default for new configurations), or from data with V1 (merchants integrated before V2). The version is shown in the Djomy developer space — ask the user which one their configuration uses, or handle both.
Never fulfill an order based on the webhook payload alone. Always call verify_payment with the transactionId to confirm status === 'SUCCESS' server-side.
You receive every event listed in eventType (payout.* only with a V2 configuration). Only act on payment.success for order fulfillment.
open_questions: The V2 payload (data.payment, data.payout) comes from Djomy's docs and has not been tested yet; the example app's webhook route (afrotools/examples shop) reads the V1 shape (data.transactionId).

Does the signature check pass on a real webhook? The maintainer received one before the v1: prefix fix of 2026-05-13 (#45, issue #44, which cites the docs' example), and its signature never matched: the example app compared the whole header until examples commit 763ab77 (2026-10-25), and that fix was checked against a computed HMAC, not a received webhook. Djomy's docs (developers.djomy.africa: the X-Webhook-Signature parameter, and hex in the « Comment générer une signature » snippets) give HMAC-SHA256 of « le payload » with the clientSecret, as v1:<signature>, without saying whether that is the raw body as webhook.signature assumes.

Does Djomy retry a delivery that failed or got no 200, and does it read the response body? The docs list the 200, 400 and 500 responses only. Return 200 quickly and confirm each payment with verify_payment rather than relying on a single delivery.
